newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: U.S. firm in oil exploration deal with Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm in oil exploration deal with Ivory Coast.

text.p: U.S. firm Global Natural Resources has signed a hydrocarbon exploration deal with Ivory Coast for offshore block CI-104, official daily Fraternite Matin said on Saturday.

It quoted company president Robert Vogt as saying that GNR would spend six billion CFA in the first phase of exploration which would involve an extensive seismic survey and well drilling. The work would be done over two years.
Block CI-104 covers a nearshore area mostly under 200 metres deep, about 170 km southwest of the commercial capital Abidjan.
GNR signed the deal on Friday, Fraternite Matin said.
It already has a 16 percent stake in a consortium exploiting oil and gas from the Lion and Panthere fields in block CI-11.

The group, led by a subsidiary of Houston-based United Meridian Corp, is producing about 20,000 barrels of oil per day and enough gas to fire a power station that has helped Ivory Coast become a net exporter of electricity.
Mines and Energy Minister Lamine Fadika said last Thursday that Shell was working with UMC in negotiating a production-sharing deal for deep-water block CI-105.
Ivory Coast has been promoting its mines and energy sector in an attempt to diversify its cocoa and coffee-based economy.
It is particularly keen to encourage exploration in deep water and included special incentives for this, like longer permit validity, in a new hydrocarbons code adopted last month.

The government says recent geological and geophysical studies have shown many very large structures in the deep offshore with estimated reserves of several billion barrels of oil and several trillion cubic feet of gas.
